study type: Mixed-methods sequential design, combining a population-based linked data cohort study, a medical record audit, and qualitative focus groups.
exposure: Maternal characteristics (primiparous, Australian born, psychiatric condition, maternal anxiety)
Obstetric interventions (caesarean section, birth in a private hospital)
Infant characteristics (preterm or early term infant, male infant, admission to SCN/NICU)
outcome: Gastro-oesophageal reflux (GOR)/Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) diagnosis/admission in the first year of life
cohort: The study included 869,188 admitted babies in New South Wales, Australia, born between 2000 and 2011, along with medical records from residential parenting centres and focus groups with nurses and doctors.
finding: Mothers with a mental health disorder were nearly five times as likely to have a baby admitted with GOR/GORD in the first year after birth.
mod_finding: Infants born via caesarean section were more likely to have a diagnostic code for GOR/GORD, suggesting a potential link through microbiome disturbance.
gest_age: Preterm or early term birth (37-38 weeks) was identified as a characteristic associated with GOR/GORD, but a specific gest_age range for the entire cohort was not mentioned.
